# FP5 diagnostics

Up: [[202310150900 Fairphone 5]] · Contrast with [[202310150907 FP5 mainline Linux gaps]]

## No error-code table exists

Fairphone states plainly that there are **no proprietary numerical fault
codes**. Failure analysis is text-based: Android logcat, Linux kernel logs,
and Qualcomm's own tooling for the modem and other low-level parts. A pop-up
reading "There has been an error" is resolved by pulling the full log over
adb, not by looking a number up in a table.

This is a useful thing to know before going looking for a code list that
does not exist.

## The built-in test mode

Reached through the MyFairphone app → "Something else" → "Internal Testing
Tool". The tests it offers, grouped:

| Group | Tests |
|---|---|
| Identity | traceability, attestation key check, camera OTP |
| Sensors | fingerprint (raw), sensor (raw), e-compass, G-sensor, gyroscope, proximity, light, backlight |
| Display and touch | LCD, LCD backlight LEDs, touch panel, touch panel (raw) |
| Cameras | front, main, ultra-wide, camera LED |
| Audio | earpiece, loudspeaker, audio, vibration |
| Radios | Bluetooth, Wi-Fi 2.4G, Wi-Fi 5G, GPS, NFC, SIM, eSIM, calling |
| Ports and power | USB/charger, USB Type-C, USB 3.0, DP video out, USB NTC, SD card, accessory |

Note what the sensor rows imply: the stock firmware can read raw values from
every sensor in [[202310150902 FP5 sensors and the low-power island]]. The
hardware works; the access path is what mainline lacks.
